page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-384-lssd is an x86_64 server instance configured for massive compute density, memory-intensive execution, and high-throughput local disk storage. The instance features 384 dedicated vCPUs alongside 3024.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero discrete GPUs available on the instance.

Integrated directly into the system is 12885 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 32 local drives. This internal NVMe array delivers direct-attached disk access without reliance on networked storage fabrics. From a resource perspective, the high consolidation of dedicated compute cores, multi-terabyte RAM, and large-scale local storage provides strong operational efficiency for large single-node environments by reducing multi-node clustering overhead and remote I/O latency. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of GPU hardware acceleration and reliance on ephemeral local storage, requiring appropriate replication strategies for persistent state.

Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-384-lssd is targeted at high-capacity transactional database engines, massive distributed in-memory data grids, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-throughput analytical workloads demanding immediate access to multi-terabyte working sets and fast scratch space.
